items.prompt: Black to move. White's pawns on d4 and e5 form a chain. Find the pawn move that attacks the base of the chain.

claims.statement: ...c5 is within 20 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16); ...a6, ...Bd7 and ...Ne7 are in the same band.
After ...c5 a black pawn attacks d4, the base of the chain.
After ...f6 a black pawn attacks e5, the head of the chain.
...f6 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: The chain runs from d4 up to e5. Which pawn is at the back, the base?
Which black pawn can attack d4 in one move?
A pawn from the c-file.
items.explain: ...c5 attacks the base d4; at depth 16 it is within 20 centipawns of the engine's best move. ...f6 attacks the head e5 instead and is rated at least 0.4 pawns lower.

feedback_by_move.f7f6: ...f6 attacks the head of the chain (e5), not the base. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.4 pawns worse than ...c5.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's pawn is still on e4 and a knight stands on c3: there is no chain. Is ...c5 rated clearly worse (0.6 pawns or more) than the engine's best move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is ...Nf6 (depth 16).
...c5 is at least 60 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
No white pawn attacks f6: there is no pawn on e5.

hints: Is there a chain here? Which white pawns stand where?
Compare with the position after 3.e5: what is different?
The base-attack idea needs a chain.
items.explain: With the pawn on e4 there is no chain, so ...c5 has no base to hit. At depth 16 the engine rates ...c5 at least 0.6 pawns worse than its first choice, ...Nf6.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn on c5 and the knight on c6 both attack d4. Find the knight move to the kingside that adds a third defender of d4.

claims.statement: The engine's first choice is Nf3 (depth 16).
Before the move two white pieces defend d4 (pawn c3 and queen).
After Nf3 three white pieces defend d4 (pawn, queen, knight).
Two black pieces attack d4 (pawn c5 and knight c6).
After Be3 three white pieces also defend d4.
After Ne2 three white pieces also defend d4.
Be3 is at least 25 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).
Ne2 is at least 25 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d4.
Which developing move puts a piece on a square that guards d4?
The knight goes to f3.
items.explain: Nf3 gives d4 three defenders against two attackers, and it is the engine's first choice at depth 16. Be3 and Ne2 also add a defender, but both are clearly worse.

items.prompt: Black to move. The pawn on c5 and the knight on c6 press on d4, and the queen stands behind the pawn. Find the pawn capture on d4.

claims.statement: ...cxd4 is within 20 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).
After ...cxd4 cxd4, two black pieces attack d4 (knight c6 and queen b6).
After ...cxd4 cxd4, two white pieces defend d4 (knight f3 and queen d1).

hints: Which black pawn can capture on the base?
After the pawn on c3 recaptures, who still attacks d4?
The c-pawn takes on d4.
items.explain: ...cxd4 cxd4 opens the queen's diagonal onto d4: the base is then attacked by knight and queen and defended by knight and queen. At depth 16 it is within 20 centipawns of the engine's best move, as are ...Nge7 and ...Nh6.

items.prompt: Black to move. The knight on c6 and the queen on b6 both attack the pawn on d4, and the capture on d4 is tempting. Find a developing move with the g8 knight.

claims.statement: The engine's first choices are ...Nh6 and ...Nge7 (within 40 centipawns, depth 16).
Two black pieces attack d4 (knight, queen).
Two white pieces defend d4 (knight, queen).
...Nxd4 is at least 300 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Count the attackers and the defenders of d4.
If you capture first and the exchanges follow, who runs out first?
Develop the g8 knight.
items.explain: d4 is attacked twice and defended twice. ...Nxd4 starts the exchanges, and the engine rates it at least 3 pawns worse than ...Nh6 or ...Nge7 at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.c6d4: ...Nxd4: d4 is attacked twice and defended twice, so the capture does not win the pawn. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 3 pawns worse than the best move.

dxc5 is at least 60 centipawns worse than the best move (depth 16).

items.explain: Be2, a3 and Bd3 are within 20 centipawns of each other at depth 16. Other quiet moves may be fine too; the app marks these three. Giving up the base with dxc5 is at least 0.6 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.d4c5: dxc5 gives up the base of the chain. At depth 16 the engine rates it at least 0.6 pawns worse than the best move.
